clue.text: PM claims love for country

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so the PM's name holds the other piece inside

parts.note: David Cameron was a British Prime Minister
love means nil in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A prime minister declares his love for his nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claims' puts O inside CAMERON.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameroon is a nation in Central Africa, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: It's the end for some home furnishings

definitions.meaning: slang for the finish or death
drapes hung at windows are household furnishings

explanation.surface: Window drapes are the last word in home decor.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses the drapes word for a fatal ending, and window drapes are a kind of soft furnishing in a house.

clue.text: Irish county has right person heading council

parts.note: Mayo is a county in the west of Ireland

explanation.surface: An Irish county has the correct person in charge of its council.
explanation.walkthrough: MAYO is a county in western Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The civic head of a town or city council is its elected leader with that title.

clue.text: Vivien, say, supports artist, one of Elizabeth's favourites

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so it comes after the other

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist
Vivien Leigh was the actress who played Scarlett O'Hara; 'say' marks her as an example of someone with that surname

explanation.surface: An actress backs a painter who was a courtier favoured by the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' puts LEIGH under RA in the down entry. Sir Walter Raleigh was a courtier and explorer favoured by Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter was a famous courtier who enjoyed the favour of Queen Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Poet about to flee pandemic

indicators.note: the abbreviation for about runs away, leaving the rest of the disease name

parts.note: Covid was the 2020 pandemic
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A poet is going to escape a global disease outbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to flee' takes C (circa) out of COVID.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was a Roman writer of verse, author of the Metamorphoses.

clue.text: Bishop enters a lounge that's brightly lit

indicators.note: the bishop's letter goes into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: to lounge is to laze about
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop walks into a sitting room full of bright light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' puts B inside A LAZE; 'lounge' looks like a room but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on fire or glowing with light is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Something baker's made with yeast rose perhaps

definitions.meaning: a large crusty loaf with diagonal slashes on top
a flower, read as something that blooms

explanation.surface: The baker's yeast dough has risen, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like the past of rise, fitting the yeast, but it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a British crusty white loaf, and whimsically any plant that blooms, such as a rose.

clue.text: Classic Jaguar car goes under bridge

indicators.note: in a down clue the car sits below the bridge, so its letters come after

parts.note: an arch is a bridge or the curved span of one
the E-Type is a famous Jaguar sports car

explanation.surface: A vintage Jaguar drives beneath a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classic' looks like a description of the Jaguar, but it is the definition, as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic is a perfect, typical model of its kind, which is what the answer means.

clue.text: Some bureaucrat arrested over document inaccuracies

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the run of letters is turned upside down, read backwards
only some of the letters of these two words are used, a run across their join

explanation.surface: A civil servant has been detained over mistakes in paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' hides ATARRE in bureaucrAT ARREsted; 'over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are a list of mistakes found in a printed text, Latin plural of erratum.

clue.text: Payments to copyright holder in Italy rose unexpectedly

indicators.note: the letters change into an arrangement nobody would predict

explanation.surface: Fees paid to an author in Italy went up by surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges ITALY ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Royalties are sums paid to an author or composer for each use or sale of their work.

clue.text: Councillor essentially avoids anxiety in retirement

indicators.note: the middle letters keep out, so they are removed from the longer word

parts.note: solicitude is anxious concern

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, its middle letters

explanation.surface: A local councillor steers clear of stress once retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes CI, the middle of Councillor; 'avoids' removes it from SOLICITUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Retirement in the sense of withdrawal from company is seclusion, being alone.

clue.text: American coach chasing very big award

indicators.note: the coach follows behind, so its letters come second

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
in America a railway carriage is called a car

explanation.surface: A US sports coach is hunting a huge prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' looks like a trainer but is a railway carriage, a car in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscar is the Academy Award statuette for film achievement.

clue.text: Skilful Anderson oddly needs time to trap India's opener

indicators.note: the letters before it close round the single letter that follows
take the letters in odd positions of the name
the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: England bowler Jimmy Anderson needs time to dismiss India's opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives ADRO from Anderson; with T it traps I, India's first letter. James Anderson is an English cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being adroit means deft and clever with the hands or mind.

clue.text: Largest threat to fruit crop?

definitions.meaning: most rounded and fat, superlative of plump
split as two words, a pest that attacks plums

explanation.surface: The biggest danger to an orchard harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second reading splits the word into PLUM PEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of plump means fattest, the most rounded, and so biggest.

clue.text: Adult joke, one described by compere as sublime

indicators.note: to be described by is to be drawn round, as a circle is described, so the host's letters go around

parts.note: MC is a master of ceremonies, a compere
A is the film rating for adult
a jest is a joke
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A master of ceremonies tells a rude joke he calls sublime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'described by' is geometry: a circle described round a figure encloses it, so the host's letters wrap the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand, stately and awe-inspiring things are called sublime or magnificent.

clue.text: Les and Tony rather agitated getting wind

indicators.note: shaken up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Two men named Les and Tony get rather worked up and flatulent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' rearranges LES TONY RATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind blowing from the north-east is named for that compass direction.

clue.text: Sorry about dog maybe biting indefinite number attending function

parts.note: RE means about or concerning

indicators.note: the pet's letters close round the next pieces like jaws

parts.note: a dog is an example of a pet

indicators.note: the function goes alongside the number, following it

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in maths
tan is the tangent, a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A dog seems sorry after biting several people at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'biting' and 'attending' are the indicators; 'function' looks like a party but is the trigonometric tangent.
explanation.definitionFit: Repentant means feeling remorse, regretful and apologetic.

clue.text: Republican appears regularly to visit pair of Americans, those seizing power

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so these letters are placed inside the doubled abbreviation
two copies of the abbreviation

parts.note: US is short for the United States

indicators.note: take every second letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Republican regularly shows up to meet two Americans, both power-grabbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'appears'; 'pair of' doubles the abbreviation and 'to visit' places the rest inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Usurpers take a throne or authority without the right to it.

clue.text: He designed spa resorts, showing stubborn nature

indicators.note: read as re-sorts, sorts again, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An architect laid out health spas and showed great obstinacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resorts' looks like holiday places but is read as re-sorts, rearranging HE DESIGNED SPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Being obstinately unwilling to change one's mind is a stubborn temperament.

clue.text: Primate is partisan when speaking

indicators.note: said out loud, one word is heard as another of different spelling

parts.note: a partisan is an irregular resistance fighter, a guerrilla

explanation.surface: An ape is biased when it talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partisan' looks like an adjective, biased, but is a resistance fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest ape is one of the primates, the order including monkeys and humans.

clue.text: Give notice a little word is misspelled

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A misspelled word is grounds to fire someone, a little.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in worD IS MISSpelled.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss an employee is to sack them, to give them notice of the end of their job.

clue.text: Blast staggering cheats

indicators.note: reeling and unsteady, so these letters lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: An exclamation of annoyance at astonishing cheats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggering' rearranges CHEATS; 'Blast' looks like an oath, but is a verb meaning harm.
explanation.definitionFit: To scathe is an old verb meaning to harm or injure, as a blast of fire does.

clue.text: Substantial account correct, yet having occasional omissions

indicators.note: every other letter is left out, keeping the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A report is weighty and accurate, though there are gaps here and there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having occasional omissions' keeps the even letters of aCcOuNtCoRrEcTyEt.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete means solid, real and tangible, rather than abstract.

clue.text: Boris frantically pens article, it indicates pressure?

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the jumbled name surrounds the article
in a frenzy, so the name's letters are thrown about

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson dashes off a newspaper column under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantically' turns BORIS into ISOBR; 'pens' puts A inside. 'pens' looks like writing but means encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather map an isobar is a line joining places of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Brother with beard displaying strength

parts.note: an awn is the bristly beard on an ear of barley or other grass

explanation.surface: A bearded brother shows off his muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beard' is the botanical one: the bristles on barley.
explanation.definitionFit: Brawn is physical muscle, sheer bodily power.

clue.text: Open University refusal to admit daughter

indicators.note: to let in, so the daughter goes inside the refusal

parts.note: no is a refusal

explanation.surface: The Open University turns down a daughter's application.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' looks part of the name Open University, but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot, button or parcel is to unfasten it, so as a verb it means to open.

clue.text: Path out of brush to cross river

indicators.note: the tail lies across the river letter, which ends up inside it

parts.note: a fox's tail is called its brush

explanation.surface: A track leads out of the undergrowth and over a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brush' looks like scrubland but is a fox's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is a track or footpath through countryside.

clue.text: Worried by honest person standing for election

indicators.note: the worry word sits beside the honest one, after it

parts.note: candid means frank and honest
ate, as in 'what's eating you', means worried

explanation.surface: An honest office-seeker is fretting.
explanation.walkthrough: ATE is the past of eat in the sense 'to bother'.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate is someone who runs for an office or seat.

clue.text: Runs special editions of newspaper

definitions.meaning: in cricket, byes, wides and no-balls are runs not credited to a batsman
additional editions printed for big news

explanation.surface: A paper prints special editions.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, extras are runs scored without the batter hitting the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket's bonus runs share their name with additional special printings of a newspaper.

clue.text: Goes along with impression voiced following trick

indicators.note: the sound piece follows the trick, coming after it

parts.note: to con is to trick

indicators.note: said aloud, the word for impressions is heard with a different spelling

parts.note: a scent is a hint or impression of something; here taken in the plural

explanation.surface: Someone agrees with an idea that a trickster expressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'voiced' turns SCENTS into the sound SENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To consent is to agree to or allow, to accept a proposal.
